Samoa / Tsunami and building fragility

From inundation
to building damage.

I reproduced the official RiskScape workflow, then progressed from building exposure to material-specific damage functions and regional consequences.

Hazard map→Building assets→Fragility→Regional impact
01

I started with exposure.

A building layer meets an externally modelled tsunami inundation raster. RiskScape samples the hazard at each asset and classifies exposure. No tsunami physics is solved in this step.

Buildings in my first QGIS output6,260
Official 50 m example reference2,059
Consequence functionExposure

Spatial sampling · NoData semantics · Resolution sensitivity

02

I inspected the model inputs.

Three data products define the experiment: inundation depth, building footprints and construction attributes, and constituency boundaries used for aggregation.

MaxEnv_All_Scenarios_50m.tifBuildings_SE_Upolu.shpSamoa_constituencies.shp

Missing asset attributes → geospatial ML

03

I traced the pipeline.

The damage-by-region model uses closest hazard sampling, chooses a consequence function, and sums the resulting per-building values by region. I kept the original model and changed only its function parameter.

sample.hazards-by = closest
analysis.function = Building_Fragility
report-event-impact.group-by[0] = area
report-event-impact.aggregate[0] = sum(consequence)

Configuration discovery → agentic workflow

04

I replaced exposure with fragility.

The official scientific functions turn inundation depth into a conditional damage probability. DS1 estimates at least light damage; DS5 estimates collapse, with curves dependent on building construction.

Fragility: DS1 and material-specific DS5 curvesAutomatically inserted from RiskScape local results when available

Parameter provenance · Fragility validation · Model uncertainty

05

I ran two expected-damage models.

The first returns the expected number of buildings reaching DS1. The second estimates DS5 collapse. These totals are model expectations, not observations from the 2009 event.

riskscape model run damage-by-region -p "analysis.function=Building_Fragility"
riskscape model run damage-by-region -p "analysis.function=Probability_of_Collapse"
Regional expected damage and collapseAutomatically inserted from RiskScape local results when available
Conditional severity comparisonAutomatically inserted from RiskScape local results when available

Automated scenario comparison · Cross-model sensitivity

06

I drew one possible outcome.

The third run samples collapse outcomes using a random draw for each building. It should not match the expected value exactly, and a single realization is not a confidence interval.

riskscape model run damage-by-region -p "analysis.function=Building_Collapse"
Expected collapse versus one stochastic realizationAutomatically inserted from RiskScape local results when available

Repeated runs · Seeds · Distributional validation

07

What this experiment established.

Data matterResolution, attributes and missingness change results.
Models matterDifferent fragility functions change the consequence.
Sampling mattersExpectation ≠ one stochastic realization.
Systems matterReusable pipelines make comparisons reproducible.

The next question is where stronger data science, autonomous research tools and social simulation could add value to this scientific pipeline.
